_comment: Evaluation-only site setup (the window the person plays in and its first steps) and answer keys for tools/evaluate_game_live.py. Never read by the game plugin: setup stands in for the person starting a game, and the oracle reads the page only to score the plugin afterwards.

ovolve_2048.oracle: () => { const size = 4, grid = Array.from({length: size}, () => Array(size).fill(0)); for (const tile of document.querySelectorAll('.tile')) { const value = +(/tile-(\d+)\b/.exec(tile.className) || [])[1]; const at = /tile-position-(\d)-(\d)/.exec(tile.className); if (value && at) { const row = +at[2] - 1, col = +at[1] - 1; grid[row][col] = Math.max(grid[row][col], value); } } const score = document.querySelector('.score-container'); const message = document.querySelector('.game-message'); return {grid, score: score ? +score.childNodes[0].textContent.trim() : null, over: !!message && message.classList.contains('game-over'), won: !!message && message.classList.contains('game-won')}; }

blockblast_org._comment: The site keeps a game in its storage and resumes it on reload: each game clears it first, as a first visit. Play opens the Unity game (about 10 s to load), then a three-placement tutorial whose drops were measured with the profile's pickup geometry (2026-11-11). No answer key: the board is a canvas.

play2048_co._comment: The site keeps a game in its storage and resumes it on reload: each game clears it first, as a first visit. A first visit opens a welcome popup over the header, closed with its x. No answer key: the board is a canvas and the page exposes no grid.

game2048_com._comment: Stage 8a control: the original open-source markup on another site (gabrielecirulli.github.io/2048 now goes to play2048.co, a development site). ovolve copied the same markup, so a result here is not counted as generalization. DOM, no start screen, ads beside the board (2026-11-12, page opened only). It saves the game in localStorage: each game clears it.

march2048_4x4._comment: Stage 8a, a DOM 2048 in its own markup (a grid of divs, each cell's text its value). No ads, no start screen, no ranking (2026-11-12, page opened only).
march2048_4x4.oracle: () => { const board = [...document.querySelectorAll('div.grid.gap-3')].find(e => e.children.length >= 9 && Number.isInteger(Math.sqrt(e.children.length))); if (!board) return null; const size = Math.sqrt(board.children.length); const values = [...board.children].map(cell => +cell.innerText.trim() || 0); return {grid: Array.from({length: size}, (_, row) => values.slice(row * size, row * size + size)), score: null, over: null, won: null}; }

arkadium_2048._comment: Stage 8a, a portal's canvas 2048 in a cross-origin iframe, its own look, with a privacy consent dialog, a pre-game video ad and a leaderboard (2026-11-12, page opened only). Setup only waits: the consent, the ad and the start are left as they are until the first approved run has seen them; keys must reach the iframe. No answer key: canvas.

doge2048._comment: Stage 8a, picture tiles (doge characters) in its own markup. A start menu: PLAY is endless play, the person's start here; Daily Drop (one official try a day) and Blitz are ranked and not played. The click was read off the 2026-11-12 screenshot at this window and is first tried on the approved run. Ads further down the page.

play2048_co_win_in_four._comment: play2048.co four merges from its win screen (plan, stage 8a): on a first visit the site imports, once, a game the original open-source 2048 saved (localStorage gameState, grid.cells[x][y]). Here 1024, 512, 256, 128 on the bottom row and a 128 above the last: 2048 takes at least four moves, so a game with no profile wins only after its three trial moves (two 1024 side by side won on the second, ending the trial, 2026-11-13). The win screen keeps the board in view under 'You Win' with a Keep Going button. A returning player's welcome popup replaces the first visit's and is left for the plugin to close. Start with --profile play2048_co --site play2048_co_win_in_four.

tatham_mines._comment: Each reload starts a new random game (9x9, 10 mines, no guessing needed). No answer key: the board is a canvas and the page exposes no grid; the end the plugin judges is compared with the status bar's.

tatham_mines_guess._comment: A game the page opens from its game id, mines placed by hand: after the start cell's opening the numbers decide no cell, the solver's least likely guess is a mine, and the page states the loss. Played with --profile tatham_mines --site tatham_mines_guess.

minesweeperonline_intermediate._comment: A classic clone: 16x16, 40 mines, cells of 16 pixels with one face colour and a raised edge on the covered ones, a count of mines and a clock above the board. Each reload starts a new game. No account; a high score is kept only when a name is typed after a fast win (never typed here). The answer key reads the page's own cells (each a div whose class says what it shows) to score readings afterwards; the harness sees pixels only.
minesweeperonline_intermediate.oracle: () => { const grid = []; for (let r = 1; document.getElementById(r + '_1') && document.getElementById(r + '_1').offsetParent !== null; r++) { const row = []; for (let c = 1; ; c++) { const cell = document.getElementById(r + '_' + c); if (!cell || cell.offsetParent === null) break; const kind = cell.className.replace('square', '').trim(); const open = /^open(\d)$/.exec(kind); row.push(open ? +open[1] : kind === 'blank' ? 9 : kind === 'bombflagged' ? 10 : kind === 'bombdeath' ? 12 : 11); } grid.push(row); } const face = document.getElementById('face').className; return {grid, score: null, over: face === 'facedead', won: face === 'facewin'}; }
